h: Getting there and making it count
p: The centre sits on the eastern edge of Winchester, up at Morn Hill just off the A31 and close to the M3, which makes it an easy run by car from Southampton, Basingstoke and beyond. If you're visiting the city by train, it's a short taxi or bus ride out from the centre rather than a stroll, so factor that into your plans.

Inside, it pays to think about what your lot will enjoy most. Little ones tend to make a beeline for the buttons and the brightly coloured hands-on bits, while older children usually get more out of the planetarium and any live demonstrations on the day. Give everyone a turn at choosing the next exhibit and you'll avoid any squabbles. A visit of two to three hours suits most families, longer if you're catching more than one show.

There's plenty more to wrap around it. In the city itself, the statue of King Alfred stands proud at the bottom of The Broadway, the ruins of Wolvesey Castle sit beside the cathedral, and Winchester City Mill, run by the National Trust, shows off a working watermill on the River Itchen. Fancy animals instead? Marwell Zoo is just south of the city at Colden Common, which makes a handy second day out if you're staying in the area. Either way, a science morning and a history afternoon is a pretty perfect Hampshire combo.
